newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmakers to begin joint Twins stadium talks.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmakers to begin joint Twins stadium talks.

text.p: Minnesota legislators have scheduled a joint House and Senate tax committee meeting on Wednesday to begin sifting through the various financing proposals for a new Twins stadium.
An obstacle to reaching a stadium deal, State House Democrat leaders have found, is that "the financing proposal changes every two days," spokesman Tom Smalec said Monday.
Legislators have floated proposals to hike taxes on cigarettes, tickets and sports merchandise to finance a new stadium, which ballclub officials have estimated could cost $400 million.
Lawmakers have also proposed special entertainment districts, expanded gambling and even partial state ownership of the team to fund the project.

Late last week, a spokesman said that Gov. Arne Carlson would not veto a bill to finance a stadium through slot machines at a racetrack if it were to pass the legislature. Carlson has stated that he would prefer to increase the cigarette tax to finance a new ballpark.
A Star-Tribune newspaper poll published on Sunday found that a majority of respondents would favor using gambling money to finance a new stadium.
The Twins current lease in the Metrodome runs through 2011, but includes an escape clause giving the team an out for poor ticket sales or if it loses money three years running.
The Twins have reported financial losses in 1995 and 1996.
